title: Market Incentives for AI Safety Investment
abstract: arXiv:2610.21607v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Despite their practical significance, modern AI systems pose significant societal risks, including toxicity, malicious use, and misinformation. Their mitigation depends not only on technical feasibility but also on the incentives of firms that develop and deploy these systems. We show how profit maximization shapes safety investment in an AI supply chain with an upstream LLM provider and several competing downstream firms. In our game-theoretic model, we derive the market-driven level of safety investment and compare it with the levels that maximize market welfare and industry profit. We find that downstream competition generally induces downstream firms to invest more in safety than the industry-profit-optimal level. By contrast, the upstream provider may underinvest relative to these benchmarks because it is not fully compensated for the surplus from safety investments. translated_abstract: 尽管现代人工智能系统具有重要的实用价值，但它们也带来了重大的社会风险，包括毒性、恶意使用和虚假信息。这些风险的缓解不仅取决于技术可行性，还取决于开发和部署这些系统的企业的激励机制。我们展示了利润最大化如何塑造一个AI供应链中的安全投资，该供应链由一个上游大语言模型提供商和若干相互竞争的下游企业组成。在我们的博弈论模型中，我们推导出市场驱动的安全投资水平，并将其与最大化市场福利和行业利润的投资水平进行比较。我们发现，下游竞争通常会促使下游企业在安全方面的投资超过行业利润最优水平。相比之下，上游提供商的投资可能低于这些基准，因为其安全投资所带来的剩余未能得到充分补偿。最后，我们分析了不同的监管干预措施如何影响……
tldr: 该研究构建了包含上游大语言模型提供商和竞争性下游企业的AI供应链博弈论模型，发现下游竞争促使下游企业的安全投资超过行业利润最优水平，而上游提供商因无法充分获得安全投资创造的剩余而倾向于投资不足。
en_tdlr: Using a game-theoretic model of an AI supply chain with an upstream LLM provider and competing downstream firms, this paper shows that downstream competition induces safety investment above the industry-profit-optimal level, while the upstream provider tends to underinvest as it is not fully compensated for the surplus generated by safety investments.
